diagrams.title: Five Checks Before You Value What You Own
diagrams.subtitle: Sum checks, NRA conversion, royalty-rate questions, live-lease proof, economic-life pricing

stages.label: Reconcile every owner decimal
stages.detail: Ann plus Bob plus Carl has to equal the lease royalty on every tract. If the sum misses, go back to the deeds.

stages.label: Convert the offer to dollars per NRA
stages.detail: 16 NMA under a 25% royalty converts to 32 NRA, so a $6,000/NMA offer ($96,000 total) is only $3,000/NRA.

stages.label: Ask which royalty rate the buyer assumed
stages.detail: On unleased minerals, if the going rate is 15-20% against the buyer's 12.5%, there is negotiation room.

stages.label: Confirm the lease is alive
stages.detail: An ORRI dies with the lease. Confirm the lease is held and the wells are economic before paying, and add washout protection to any assignment.

stages.label: Price to remaining economic life
stages.detail: Review declines, reserves, operators, rights and lease terms. On an old single well, value the override on existing production only.

diagrams.caption: Street math runs on net mineral acres, the royalty decimal and net royalty acres. A headline per-NMA offer can halve once normalized to the 1/8 standard.
diagrams.assumptions_note: All figures are the speakers' own worked examples. The 16 NMA, 25% royalty and $6,000/NMA offer come from a single Matt Sands illustration and are not market quotes.
diagrams.note: Attributed to LMJ Land Services (IBxLIQjDNto), Matt Sands (iVFjOPF8JW0, pjmqehPUgL8), Blue Mesa Minerals (PR8LyKmo8S4) and PetroPeak Investments LLC (zHSS1bvXiNk) on YouTube.

diagrams.title: The Title Cost Ladder From Guesswork to Courthouse Search
diagrams.subtitle: What a mistake, a probate and a records search each cost

stages.label: Guessed title call
stages.conversion: Avoided by working every interest in fractions and never guessing
stages.detail: The Landman Class instructor cites mistakes of this size and says one guess can lose the client and the whole firm's jobs.

stages.label: Simple probate as curative
stages.conversion: Can exceed the value of a 0.1 net-acre interest
stages.detail: Matt Sands and Justin Williams note this is why affidavits of heirship get used. Ask the operator which document it will accept before drafting.

stages.label: File Viewer document package
stages.conversion: Pull only the instruments the chain actually needs
stages.detail: Digital courthouse tool cited alongside Courthouse Direct for title runs.

stages.label: Courthouse Direct legal-description search
stages.conversion: Treat a zero-result search as an input error first
stages.detail: Paul Cones ran a live Reeves County search and read out the charge after first typing an entry into the wrong box.

stages.label: Courthouse Direct base fee
stages.detail: Clean title runs take 1-2 weeks, complex chains 3-5 weeks.

diagrams.caption: A search costs tens of dollars, curative costs thousands, and a guessed fraction costs hundreds of thousands.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Stages are ordered by cost, not by workflow volume. Where a range was quoted, the value uses the high end of that range.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Landman Class (ibeQr-rDmZ4), Matt Sands with Justin Williams (sB8BNPnN_Os, zoP-dgL5D7M) and CourthouseAcademy with Paul Cones (822U1_i8V5Q) on YouTube.

diagrams.title: From Mineral Value to the Bonus Actually Offered
diagrams.subtitle: Matt Sands' divide-by-2-or-3 rule against a Nacogdoches Haynesville offer

bars.label: Divide by 2 for the top of range

diagrams.caption: Sands prices a fair bonus at mineral value divided by 2 or 3, so $3,000/NMA minerals support about $1,000/acre, far above the $300/NMA offer on the table.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The $3,000, $1,000 and $300 figures are Sands' own. The $1,500 step and the deductions are simple arithmetic on those figures. Sands still favors the highest royalty rate over bonus.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Matt Sands (xiP5PiaaYKE, qru8bh4mMms) on YouTube, answering a Nacogdoches County Haynesville lease offer.

diagrams.title: What It Costs to Know What You Own
diagrams.subtitle: State data paywalls, well software, consultants, landmen and title searches
diagrams.unit: US dollars at the quoted billing basis

bars.label: WellDatabase Essential plan
bars.display: $250 per month per user, up to 10,000 wells exported

diagrams.caption: Sands paid one month of WellDatabase Essential for decline curve work, downgraded to free, and replaced a $600 to $800 consultant.

diagrams.title: Four Gates Before a Division Order Gets Signed
diagrams.subtitle: Rebuild the decimal, strike the extras, return the W-9, watch operator changes

nodes.question: Does your rebuilt decimal (NMA divided by unit acres times royalty) match the order?
nodes.fail_action: Call the division order department, tell them they made a mistake or to convince you otherwise, and ask for the redacted title opinion pages covering your interest.

nodes.question: Is the order free of extra clauses, operator-liability terms and cost-deduction language?
nodes.fail_action: On a Texas order, strike and initial every clause beyond the statutory list and return with proof of delivery, or substitute the NADOA model form.

nodes.question: Is a W-9 on file with the paying company?
nodes.fail_action: Return the W-9 no matter what, even on Oklahoma wells you refuse to sign, to avoid roughly 28% backup withholding.

nodes.question: Does the decimal hold when a new operator sends its own order?
nodes.pass_next: Sign, then keep checking each stub against the lease fraction
nodes.fail_action: Treat the change as a red flag and make the new operator show how it built the number.

diagrams.caption: Matt Sands' benchmark is 160/1,280 times 18.75%, or 0.0234375. Mineral View shows that a half-size decimal on a $100,000-a-month well costs $187,500 over 20 years.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Blue Mesa Minerals reports problems with maybe 2 of about 130 operators on the NADOA form. Richard Winblad advises never signing even that form in Oklahoma, citing 12% interest compounded annually on late pay.
diagrams.note: Attributed to NARO (W3POOsq6ka0), Matt Sands (tJr4jiz31fw), Royalty Clerk (DN-VIoSmyF0, blbomhUd0sA), Blue Mesa Minerals (SfX6ycoYg24), Richard Winblad (iD4uCjptCXM) and Mineral View (KYu7M4t5LAk) on YouTube.

diagrams.title: The Operator Desk Facing the Permit and Docket Clock
diagrams.subtitle: Bonding, testimony, gas composition and facilities around one regulatory lead

center.focus: The permit and the docket clock control the money. Operator witnesses ask for roughly 90-day windows rather than 30.

spokes.kpi: Marginal and inactive share checked against the 15% trigger before signing; McGowan's 100-well example hit $15 million overnight
Redline reconciled with direct testimony and every exhibit cost line audited; Devon had to explain $1.27 million that was really the $1.3 million credit
Sour gas checked against the 10,000 ppm takeaway limit; Devon faced roughly 13,500 ppm
About $350,000 avoided by tying new horizontals into existing facilities

diagrams.caption: Tiered blanket bonds run from $150,000 for 1-5 wells up to $1 million for 26-plus wells, while public commenters put average plugging at $163,000.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The roles are an organizing frame for the testified gates, not a staffing plan any speaker described. Every number is quoted from hearing testimony or operator statements.
diagrams.note: Attributed to New Mexico Oil Conservation Commission hearings (gfqoliQ78bk, -7pNwWErBfk), OCD Pecos Hall (Gyi9ijeMNgA) and Alpha Seven Energy (gjm7ZmMazmc) on YouTube.

diagrams.title: Net Revenue Interest From Lessee to Pooled Owner
diagrams.subtitle: How royalties, overrides and pooling carve the decimal

buckets.label: Lessee NRI under a 1/8 lease
buckets.notes: 100% WI after the lease, less the 1/8 royalty (Alyce Hoge drills).

buckets.label: Lessee NRI under a 3/16 lease
buckets.notes: A higher royalty leaves less for the operator before any override or NPRI.

buckets.label: Sunrise lease pooled into a 320-acre unit
buckets.notes: 82.5 cents per dollar after a 12.5% royalty and 5% override, then 0.20625 once 80 acres are pooled into 320.

buckets.label: Bakken owner in a 1,280-acre DSU
buckets.notes: 16 NMA divided by 1,280 times 15%. About $937 on 10,000 barrels at $50 over three months.

diagrams.caption: Every division-order decimal is built by multiplication. Run the check and balance lease by lease, and challenge the operator when your number does not match.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Each bucket is a separate worked example, not one shared property. Sands notes Bakken barrels bring $50 against $60 WTI because of the price differential.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Matt Sands (Yy7az5T7_vs), Land Training www.landtraining.net (eZU5hvGcngg) and UHD Continuing and Professional Education (oHKF06pFkh0) on YouTube.

diagrams.title: Four Weeks to Act on Mineral Market Moves
diagrams.subtitle: Deductions, pricing, operator capital and new-gas offers

weeks.title: Audit deductions on every statement
weeks.deliverable: Post-production deductions (20% to 35%) compared against the lease's gross-proceeds language
weeks.gate: Flywheel deducted under a net-proceeds statute despite gross proceeds leases until a court ruling stopped it

weeks.title: Reprice royalties off the futures strip
weeks.deliverable: Strip minus basis, set against buyers anchoring on $50 to $70 oil
weeks.gate: No household budget on spot spikes; checks reflect a monthly weighted average and arrive about two months late

weeks.title: Read the operator's investor presentation
weeks.deliverable: Where cash flow and rigs are actually going, beyond the headlines
weeks.gate: Expect buybacks and dividends first and a one to two quarter lag before rigs respond

weeks.title: Screen helium, pipeline and re-promoter offers
weeks.deliverable: Scout cards scanned for non-flammable gas, measured against Rynott's 0.5% to 1.5% helium, 3 to 6 MMcf/d and 10 to 20 location screen
weeks.gate: No helium lease to a re-promoter, and no blind pipeline final offer; a $21,000 offer became about a $7M verdict while typical protesters win 10% to 20% more

diagrams.caption: Price spikes reach royalty checks about two months late, and rigs respond one to two quarters later, so act on statements and operator plans rather than headlines.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The weekly sequence is an organizing frame for the testified checks. The Matterhorn award is under appeal, and the long-term oil view ranges from Sands' $60 to $70 to Josh Young's roughly $105.
diagrams.note: Attributed to Matt Sands with Justin Williams (n2MrqKJ_h80, M3eFdVkW_mY, oHhvtjxLX9c, FDXztudBSFk, ptrz57qzl54), guest Tim Rynott and Bison Interests' Josh Young on YouTube.
